proposals.title: Actor identifier is populated
proposals.description: Require every actor identifier to be non-null so each record can be addressed reliably.
evidence: Schema marks actor.actor_id as a non-null integer primary key.
Profile reports 10 rows, 10 non-null values, and 0 nulls.
assumptions: The primary-key metadata represents the intended record identifier.

proposals.title: Actor identifier is unique
proposals.description: Require actor identifiers to be unique across the table.
evidence: Schema labels actor.actor_id as the primary key.
Uniqueness metric evaluated 10 values with 10 passing and 0 violations.
assumptions: Each actor row is intended to have a distinct identifier.

proposals.title: Clarify whether actor first name is mandatory
proposals.description: The column appears to contain a first-name component, but its optionality needs a business decision before enforcing completeness.
evidence: Schema defines actor.first_name as nullable text.
Profile reports 9 non-null values and 1 null among 10 rows.
assumptions: The identifier may describe a personal-name field, but identifiers are treated as untrusted metadata.

proposals.title: Document actor last-name semantics
proposals.description: Confirm whether this text field is a required family-name component and whether naming conventions permit blanks or single-part names.
evidence: Schema defines actor.last_name as nullable text.
Profile reports 10 non-null and 10 distinct values among 10 rows.
assumptions: Observed completeness does not by itself establish a mandatory-name policy.

proposals.title: Clarify whether film titles must be unique

Schema does not mark film.title as a key.
assumptions: A repeated title may be valid, so distinct-count evidence is insufficient for a uniqueness policy.

proposals.title: Rental rate is nonnegative
proposals.description: Require the numeric rate to be zero or greater, subject to confirmation that the field represents a charge rather than an adjustment.
evidence: Schema defines film.rental_rate as decimal.
Profile reports 10 non-null values and 4 distinct values; the guarded sample confirms numeric shape.
assumptions: If the field represents a charge, negative values are not valid.

proposals.title: Define the film rating vocabulary

evidence: Schema defines film.rating as nullable text.
Profile reports 10 non-null values and 6 distinct values; the guarded sample exposes only a short-string shape and no raw labels.
assumptions: A controlled vocabulary may exist, but its members cannot be inferred safely from metadata or redacted samples.
